name: Cohort Retention Decay Curve Analysis
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that our product delivers sustained, long-term utility to users. We will verify this by tracking weekly active usage across monthly cohorts, and consider it validated if the retention curve flattens into a stable horizontal asymptote at ≥ 20% weekly active retention by Week 8: lim R(t) as t → ∞  ≥ 0.20
schematic: Week 8 retention on the decay curve

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Define the core action that means real value - exporting a project, working with a teammate - not a login.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Group users into weekly or monthly cohorts by the week they finished onboarding and follow them.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Plot retention per cohort and watch whether the curve flattens or keeps decaying toward zero.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Define the core engagement action that reflects genuine product value (e.g., exporting a project or collaborating with a teammate), rather than simply logging in.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Group users into discrete cohorts based on the calendar week or month they completed onboarding. Track their activity over time.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Plot percentage retention curves for each cohort over time, tracking whether the retention trajectory flattens or continues decaying toward the origin.

warning.label: The Walking Dead Metric Trap
warning.text: Top-line registered users can grow while every cohort decays to zero; growth stalls when spend slows.

warningFull: A company can show impressive top-line growth in total registered users while its underlying cohort retention curves decay steadily to zero, meaning growth will stall the moment acquisition spend slows.
